t.7.99.1: When the night had brightened into dawn, Rāma, broad-chested and of great renown, with eyes like lotus petals, then spoke to the family priest.
t.7.99.3: Then the radiant Vasiṣṭha performed, duly and without omitting anything, the entire righteous rite of the great departure.
t.7.99.2: Let the agnihotra, with its ghee and blazing fire, go on ahead, and let the parasol of the Vājapeya and the splendid conveyance proceed along the great road.
t.7.99.4: Then, clad in garments of linen and reciting the supreme Brahman, he took kuśa grass in both his hands and, wholly intent upon it, set forth.
t.7.99.6: At Rāma's left side stood Śrī, the lotus-dwelling goddess, fully composed; on his right was large-eyed Hrī, Modesty, and likewise Resolve went before him.
t.7.99.5: Speaking not a word to anyone, unmoved and joyless on the road, he went forth from that house, blazing like the radiant sun.
t.7.99.7: Arrows of many kinds, and the bow with its long, stretched frame, all of them in human form, follow Kākutstha.
t.7.99.8: The Vedas in the form of brāhmaṇas, Sāvitrī the protector of all, the syllable Oṃ and the exclamation Vaṣaṭ, all followed devotedly after Rāma.
t.7.99.9: The great-souled sages, and indeed all the brahmins as well, followed Kākutstha as he approached the gate of heaven.
t.7.99.10: As he went, the women who dwelt in the inner apartments followed him, accompanied by their maidservants, old and young, and by eunuchs and attendants.
t.7.99.12: Then the great-souled Brahmins, carrying their sacred fires and composed in mind, followed the wise Kākutstha together with their sons and wives.
t.7.99.11: Bharata, together with the women of the inner apartments and accompanied by Śatrughna, went forth; having taken up Rāma's vow, they all followed Rāghava in devotion.
t.7.99.13: The ministers and the bands of servants, all together with their sons, with their kinsmen and with their followers, followed Rāghava as if overjoyed.
t.7.99.14: Then all the subjects, surrounded by joyful and well-nourished people, their hearts won over by his virtues, followed Rāghava as he went forth.
t.7.99.16: No one there was downcast, ashamed, or sorrowful. Everything was joyful and delighted, utterly wondrous.
t.7.99.15: All of that host, bathed and rejoicing, bright with flowers and unsurpassed, all of it exuberant with cries of kilikilā, was devoted to Rāma.
t.7.99.17: Then the people of the countryside, desiring to see the king's departure, arrived; and they too, upon merely seeing it, followed along together with all the others, devoted to him.
t.7.99.18: The bears, monkeys and rākṣasas, and the people dwelling in the city, followed behind with supreme devotion, their minds wholly composed.
